# Quick Brief: Exit-Ticket Frequency Decision

## Summary

The team must decide by Friday whether to run exit tickets daily or weekly this term. Daily exit tickets give faster feedback loops but cost more class time. Weekly tickets save roughly twenty minutes per week but slow the feedback loop. Two recent studies and one practitioner guide support daily use with a two-question cap [1]. The two-question cap keeps completion under three minutes [2]. Weekly checks remain adequate for stable content.

## Key Points

- Daily two-question exit tickets improve retention of covered material [1].
- Completion stays under three minutes when the ticket holds two questions [2].
- Weekly checks suit content that changes little between lessons [3].
- The deciding factor is how often new material introduces confusion.

## Action Items

- Adopt daily exit tickets with a maximum of two questions.
- Review the weekly aggregate every Friday during planning period.
- Revisit the decision at half term with the retention data.

## Bibliography
[1] Author, A. (2024). Retrieval pace and retention in classroom practice. Journal of Classroom Studies.
[2] Author, B. (2023). Time cost of formative checks in elementary grades. Applied Education Notes.
[3] Author, C. (2022). Feedback frequency for stable curricula. Teaching Notes Quarterly.
